facts.statement: The genus Anthropornis was described by Wiman in 1905.
Anthropornis measured 1.8 meters in length and weighed 90 kilograms.
facts.quote: Anthropornis reached 1.8 m in length from the tip of the beak to the tip of the tail, and 90 kg in weight

facts.statement: Anthropornis was the largest penguin species of the Eocene epoch.
facts.quote: making it the largest penguin of the Eocene epoch.

facts.statement: One specimen of Anthropornis is estimated to have reached a body length of 2.05 meters and a weight of 108 kilograms.
facts.quote: There is also an estimate that one specimen of Anthropornis could have reached a body length of 2.05 m and 108 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Fossils of Anthropornis have been found in the La Meseta Formation on Seymour Island off Antarctica and in New Zealand.
facts.quote: Fossils of it have been found in the La Meseta Formation on Seymour Island off the coast of Antarctica and in New Zealand.

facts.statement: The type species Anthropornis nordenskjoldi possessed a bent joint in its wing, likely a vestigial trait inherited from flying ancestors.
facts.quote: The type species, Anthropornis nordenskjoldi, had a bent joint in the wing, probably a vestigial trait from its flying ancestors.

facts.statement: Anthropornis is classified within the family Spheniscidae.
Anthropornis lived between 45 and 37 million years ago during the Late Eocene and early Oligocene.
facts.quote: Anthropornis es un género extinto de pingüino que vivió hace entre 45 a 37 millones de años, durante el Eoceno tardío y la parte inicial del Oligoceno.

facts.statement: Anthropornis reached a height of 1.7 meters and weighed up to 90 kilograms.
facts.quote: Alcanzaba 1.7 metros de altura y llegaba a pesar 90 kg.

facts.statement: The time range for Anthropornis is recorded as the Bartonian to Burdigalian stages, from 41.03 to 15.98 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bartonian to Burdigalian (41.03 to 15.98 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Anthropornis lived between 45 and 33 million years ago during the Late Eocene and early Oligocene.
rejected.quote: Anthropornis is a genus of giant penguin that lived 45-33 million years ago, during the Late Eocene and the earliest part of the Oligocene.
